meta.title: Money Basics — the things school never taught
meta.disclaimer: Educational only — not financial, legal, tax or Syariah advice. Verify current figures with the official source before acting.

categories.title: Your credit record
categories.intro: The history banks read before they decide what to offer you.

lessons.oneLiner: Your 12-month loan report card, kept by Bank Negara.
lessons.body: CCRIS lists your loans, cards and financing and shows whether you paid on time using simple monthly codes. PTPTN loans can appear here too.
lessons.whyItMatters: Banks pull CCRIS before approving a loan or card. Arrears can lead to a conditional decline.
lessons.quickTip: Check your record through the official eCCRIS channel and fix errors early.

lessons.oneLiner: A 300–850 signal of how risky your credit profile looks.
lessons.body: CTOS is a private credit agency. Payment history is the largest factor at about 45%, followed by amounts owed, credit mix, new credit and history length.
lessons.whyItMatters: A stronger score can make approvals easier and protect your rate spread.
lessons.quickTip: Pay on time, keep card balances below 30% of the limit and avoid many applications at once.

lessons.oneLiner: How much of your income already goes to debt.
lessons.body: DSR is monthly debt commitments divided by income. This app shows a planning view on net income because statutory deductions change the headroom you really have.
lessons.whyItMatters: Every existing commitment, including PTPTN and assigned card limits, can reduce future borrowing capacity.
lessons.quickTip: Clear small debts before applying for a large home or car loan.

categories.title: Borrowing smart
categories.intro: Debt is a tool; expensive or unclear debt is the trap.

lessons.oneLiner: Zero interest only when you clear the full statement.
lessons.body: Pay the full statement by the due date and the grace period can keep retail purchases interest-free. Carrying a balance can trigger interest of up to 18% a year.
lessons.whyItMatters: Minimum payments can stretch a RM5,000 balance across years and add a large finance charge.
lessons.quickTip: Set autopay for the full statement, not only the minimum.

lessons.oneLiner: 0% interest — until a late fee changes the maths.
lessons.body: BNPL can be interest-free when paid on time. A flat late fee on a small purchase can become an extreme effective APR, and several plans fragment cashflow.
lessons.whyItMatters: A RM10 fee on a RM100 purchase paid two weeks late is about 260% effective APR.
lessons.quickTip: If you cannot pay the full price today, you cannot afford the purchase yet.

lessons.oneLiner: The same percentage can represent very different costs.
lessons.body: A reducing-balance rate charges interest on what remains. A flat rate charges against the original amount for the whole tenure, so the headline percentage looks smaller.
lessons.whyItMatters: Comparing flat and reducing rates directly can make the cheaper-looking loan cost more.
lessons.quickTip: Ask for the EIR and compare like with like.

lessons.oneLiner: The truer yearly cost to compare across loan offers.
lessons.body: EIR expresses the payment stream on a reducing-balance basis. A 3% flat car quote can be around 5% EIR; a 6% flat personal loan can be around 11% EIR.
lessons.whyItMatters: Two providers can advertise similar flat rates but produce different true costs.
lessons.quickTip: Choose the offer with the clearest EIR, fees and product disclosure sheet.

categories.title: Income tax, simply
categories.intro: A few plain-language rules make tax less mysterious.

lessons.oneLiner: The filing threshold and reliefs decide the answer.
lessons.body: Salaried taxpayers generally file through MyTax. A common planning threshold after EPF is around RM37,333 a year, but your exact position depends on reliefs and income sources.
lessons.whyItMatters: Filing can reconcile PCB and recover a refund when too much was deducted.
lessons.quickTip: Register early and keep receipts for relief claims.

lessons.oneLiner: An advance tax payment taken from salary each month.
lessons.body: PCB is paid to LHDN on your behalf. Your annual filing reconciles the amount: overpayment may be refunded and underpayment may need a top-up.
lessons.whyItMatters: Ignoring filing can leave a refund or a correction unresolved.
lessons.quickTip: Keep your EA form and relief receipts together throughout the year.

lessons.oneLiner: Legal deductions that reduce chargeable income.
lessons.body: Common reliefs include the individual relief, EPF and life insurance/takaful, lifestyle items and qualifying education or medical claims. First-home loan interest relief can reach RM7,000 or RM5,000 a year in the qualifying window.
lessons.whyItMatters: Reliefs reduce the income on which progressive tax is calculated.
lessons.quickTip: Claim only eligible items and keep the supporting records.

lessons.oneLiner: Submit salaried Form BE online, usually by 30 April.
lessons.body: MyTax is the online filing channel for individual income tax. Deadlines vary by form and year, so check the latest LHDN announcement.
lessons.whyItMatters: Late filing can create penalties and unnecessary stress.
lessons.quickTip: Set a reminder before the deadline and submit even when you expect a refund.

categories.title: Retirement & protection
categories.intro: Protect the income and people your plans depend on.

lessons.oneLiner: Your long-term retirement contribution and safety net.
lessons.body: Employee EPF contributions are commonly modelled at 11% in this app. EPF can also support certain housing withdrawals under the official rules.
lessons.whyItMatters: A down payment decision should not accidentally trade away every long-term buffer.
lessons.quickTip: Treat EPF withdrawals as an offset to cash needed, not as a discount to the loan contract.

lessons.oneLiner: Statutory protection contributions that reduce take-home pay.
lessons.body: The calculator estimates employee SOCSO and EIS on a capped wage basis. Your payslip and current PERKESO schedule are the source of truth.
lessons.whyItMatters: Net income gives a more realistic DSR view than gross income alone.
lessons.quickTip: Use your actual PCB and payslip deductions when comparing affordability.

lessons.oneLiner: Cover the household before stretching the household budget.
lessons.body: MRTA/MRTT usually reduces with the loan and can be paid cash or capitalised. MLTA/MLTT is typically level, portable and paid separately. Islamic products use takaful terminology.
lessons.whyItMatters: A rate comparison that ignores protection can understate the real monthly plan.
lessons.quickTip: Ask what is included, whether the premium is financed and whether the cover is portable.

categories.title: Money habits that compound
categories.intro: Small recurring choices become large numbers over time.

lessons.oneLiner: A simple starting frame for needs, wants and goals.
lessons.body: Use 50/30/20 as a flexible prompt, not a law: needs first, wants second, savings or debt reduction third. Your household and income may need a different mix.
lessons.whyItMatters: A named plan makes room for savings before the month disappears.
lessons.quickTip: Automate the goal amount on salary day and review it after three months.

lessons.oneLiner: Cash that keeps one surprise from becoming expensive debt.
lessons.body: A common planning target is 3–6 months of essential expenses in accessible savings. Start with one month if that is what is realistic.
lessons.whyItMatters: A buffer reduces the need to use cards, BNPL or a personal loan during a shock.
lessons.quickTip: Name the account and automate a small weekly or monthly transfer.

lessons.oneLiner: Returns can earn returns; debt can compound against you.
lessons.body: A recurring saving can grow through contributions plus growth. The same curve shows why unpaid high-interest debt balloons when interest is added repeatedly.
lessons.whyItMatters: Time can work for you when saving and against you when revolving debt remains unpaid.
lessons.quickTip: Use the visualizer: compare RM200 a month invested with RM5,000 carried at 18%.

lessons.oneLiner: The same ringgit usually buys less over time.
lessons.body: Inflation is the broad rise in prices. A plan should leave room for rising essentials instead of assuming today's budget stays fixed for decades.
lessons.whyItMatters: A long loan and a long savings goal both need realistic future costs.
lessons.quickTip: Review subscriptions, insurance and emergency-fund targets once a year.
